question:
Choose the idiom / phrase that can substitute the highlighted group of words meaningfully.

Everyone around me has **ignored** my plea.

options.text: Let the cat out of the bag

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Turn a deaf ear"** means to deliberately ignore someone or something. (अनसुना करना)

 
 
• **Example: **Despite her pleas for help, her colleagues turned a deaf ear to her.
 
 
 
• **"Turn a deaf ear"** can be used in contexts where someone is being ignored or not listened to, fitting perfectly with the given sentence. (अनसुना करना)
 
 
• **Example: **Everyone around me has turned a deaf ear to my plea.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Let the cat out of the bag** (राज़ खोल देना): To reveal a secret or disclose something that was supposed to be kept confidential.

 
 
• **Example:** He let the cat out of the bag about the surprise party.
 
 
 
• **Spill the beans** (सच्चाई उजागर करना): To reveal secret information unintentionally or indiscreetly.
 
 
• **Example:** She accidentally spilled the beans about the company's new product launch.
 
 
 
• **Twist my arm** (दबाव डालना): To pressure or coerce someone into doing something.
 
 
• **Example:** They didn't have to twist my arm to get me to join the team.
